subject.title: [Feature]: Session busy status reply + cancel option during long-running model responses

question: What canonical busy-session UX should OpenClaw expose when a new channel message arrives while that same session is already running?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but accepting it adds cross-channel user-visible behavior and likely new text/action/config semantics, so automation should not choose the product contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve generic busy acknowledgement
options.body: Define a core scripted busy reply with stable reason metadata and conservative channel-safe `/stop` and `/new` guidance, then implement it through queue policy, runner return payloads, dispatch, and channel proof.

options.title: Keep typing/status-only behavior
options.body: Keep current queued-followup typing/status signals as the intended UX and close or narrow the scripted-reply request after documenting that decision.

options.title: Defer behind activity API
options.body: Wait for the broader gateway activity/attention contract in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/39127, then build channel replies from that canonical state model.

recommendation.title: Approve generic busy acknowledgement
recommendation.body: Define a core scripted busy reply with stable reason metadata and conservative channel-safe `/stop` and `/new` guidance, then implement it through queue policy, runner return payloads, dispatch, and channel proof.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest recent history on the queue policy, queued-followup, and typing mitigation paths that this contract would change.
